### Reading, Converting, Analyzing and Plotting ADORA1 E3 and E4 
### Administered Rats 
#### Reading in ADORA1 E3 and E4 Administered Rat Data for 
#### E3 and rLEN
```{r}
# Reading  ADORA1 Administered Rats
readxl::read_excel(path ="../Copy of analysis_SCN.xlsx",
                   sheet = "ADORA1",
                    range ="A1:M40") ->  Circadian_ADORA1

 Circadian_ADORA1 %>%
  select(`Animal ID`,`Time point`, `Group`, `Normalized fold change`) %>%
  rename("ID" = `Animal ID`, "Time" = `Time point`,
        "Change" = `Normalized fold change`)->  Circadian_ADORA1


# Check if 'Normalized fold change' is character and needs parsing
if (is.character( Circadian_ADORA1$Change)) {
   Circadian_ADORA1 <-  Circadian_ADORA1 %>%
    mutate(Change = parse_number(Change))
}

# Separating E3 data and pivoting
 Circadian_ADORA1_E3 <-  Circadian_ADORA1 %>%
  filter(grepl("E3", Group)) %>%
  mutate(
    Time = recode(Time,
    "ZT0" = "0", "ZT6" = "6", "ZT12" = "12", "ZT18" = "18", "ZT24" = "24")
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = ID,
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = Change) %>%
  select(-c(ID))
if (!"24" %in% colnames( Circadian_ADORA1_E3)) {
   E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter <-  Circadian_ADORA1_E3 %>%
    mutate(`24` = `0`)}

# Separating E4 data and pivoting    
 Circadian_ADORA1_E4 <-  Circadian_ADORA1 %>%
  filter(grepl("E4", Group)) %>%
  mutate(
    Time = recode(Time,
    "ZT0" = "0", "ZT6" = "6", "ZT12" = "12", "ZT18" = "18", "ZT24" = "24")
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = ID,
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = Change)%>%
  select(-c(ID))
if (!"24" %in% colnames( Circadian_ADORA1_E4)) {
   E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter <-  Circadian_ADORA1_E4 %>%
    mutate(`24` = `0`)}
```


#### Converting Data into Usable Format for Extracting VOIs and Plotting
```{r}
# Data Conversion to get Individual Points for ADORA1 E3
# Rat Model
## X value is Zeitgeber time,  Y value is # of Fold Changes

# Loads Initial Dataset for E3 ADORA1 E3 and E4 Rats and 
# Removes Outliers
#outlier_detection(Circadian_ADORA1_E3) -> out_res_E3ADORA1
#filter_outliers(Circadian_ADORA1_E3, 
#                out_res_E3ADORA1) ->  E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter

# Performs Data Carpentry on Filtered E3 ADORA1 Dataset and Removes 'NA's,
## filters out ZT of 24
E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`0`,`6`,`12`, `18`, `24`), names_to = "ZT", 
               values_to = "Fold_Changes") %>%
  drop_na(`Fold_Changes`) %>%
  mutate(ZT = as.numeric(ZT)) %>%
  arrange(ZT) -> E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter
E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter %>%
  # Filter out ZT of 24
  filter(ZT != 24)  -> E3_Circadian_ADORA1_data

# Creating Cosinor Model for E3 ADORA1 Rat Plots
cosinor.lm(`Fold_Changes` ~ time(ZT), period = 24,
           data = E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter) -> cosMod_E3_ADORA1
# Creating Cosinor Model for E3 ADORA1 Rat Data Analysis
cosinor.lm(`Fold_Changes` ~ time(ZT), period = 24,
           data = E3_Circadian_ADORA1_data) -> cosMod_E3_ADORA1_data
```

```{r}
# Data Conversion to get Individual Points for ADORA1 E4 
# Rat Model X value is Zeitgeber time,  Y value is # of Fold Changes

# Loads Initial Dataset for E4 ADORA1 E3 and E4 Rats and Removes Outliers
# outlier_detection(Circadian_ADORA1_E4) -> out_res_E4ADORA1
# filter_outliers(Circadian_ADORA1_E4, 
#                out_res_E4ADORA1) ->  E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter

# Performs Data Carpentry on Filtered E3 ADORA1 Dataset and Removes 'NA's
E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`0`,`6`,`12`, `18`, `24`), names_to = "ZT", 
               values_to = "Fold_Changes") %>%
  drop_na(`Fold_Changes`) %>%
  mutate(ZT = as.numeric(ZT)) %>%
  arrange(ZT) -> E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter
E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter %>%
  # Filter out ZT of 24
  filter(ZT != 24)  -> E4_Circadian_ADORA1_data

# Creating Cosinor Model for E3 ADORA1 Rat Plots
cosinor.lm(`Fold_Changes` ~ time(ZT), period = 24,
           data = E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter) -> cosMod_E4_ADORA1
# Creating Cosinor Model for E3 ADORA1 Rat Plot Data Analysis
cosinor.lm(`Fold_Changes` ~ time(ZT), period = 24,
           data = E4_Circadian_ADORA1_data) -> cosMod_E4_ADORA1_data
```


#### Calculating the Y-limits for Plots of Cosinor Fit
```{r}
# Finding the max Y-value Across Both Datsets in Order to Set Y-limits of 
# Future Plot
max(E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter$`Fold_Changes`, 
    E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter$`Fold_Changes`) -> ADORA1_max
# Calculate y_peak based on ADORA1_max
if (ADORA1_max < 3) {
  y_peak <- ceiling(ADORA1_max / 0.25) * 0.25 
  } else {
  y_peak <- ceiling(ADORA1_max / 5) * 5}
```


#### Creating Plots of Original Data with Cosinor Fit Overlayed for Rat Models
```{r}
# Creating Individual Plots of Rat Datasets w/ Cosinor Fits
## Loads Function plot_cosinor_clock Into Global Environment, Which Takes cosMod 
## Model, Original Dataset, Plot Title and Desired x-breaks (currently set for
## Zetigeber Time, to see how to change to regular time see function notes) and
## Generates Plot of Original Data with Overlayed Cosinor Fit Model

# Creating Plot for E3 ADORA1 Rat Model
plot_cosinor_clock(cosMod_E3_ADORA1, E3_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter, 
             "ADORA1 E3", "E3",
             x_breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6)) -> mod_plot_E3_ADORA1


# Creating Plot for E4 ADORA1 Rat Model
plot_cosinor_clock(cosMod_E4_ADORA1, E4_Circadian_ADORA1_Filter, 
             "ADORA1 E4", "E4",
             x_breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6)) -> mod_plot_E4_ADORA1
```

#### Generation of Pseudo-Rayleigh Plots
```{r}
#### Creating a Combined Pseudo-Rayleigh Plot for Group Rhythm Visualization
# --- Data Extraction ---
# Extract E3 ADORA1 (ADORA1) data
E3_ADORA1_acrophase <- E3_ADORA1_Results_table$Values[E3_ADORA1_Results_table$Parameter == "E3 Acrophase (Hrs)"]
E3_ADORA1_amplitude <- E3_ADORA1_Results_table$Values[E3_ADORA1_Results_table$Parameter == "E3 Amplitude"]

# Extract E4 ADORA1 (ADORA1) data
E4_ADORA1_acrophase <- E4_ADORA1_Results_table$Values[E4_ADORA1_Results_table$Parameter == "E4 Acrophase (Hrs)"]
E4_ADORA1_amplitude <- E4_ADORA1_Results_table$Values[E4_ADORA1_Results_table$Parameter == "E4 Amplitude"]

# --- Data Preparation for Combined Plot ---
# Create data frames for each condition
E3_ADORA1_vector_data <- data.frame(
  Condition = "E3",
  acrophase = E3_ADORA1_acrophase,
  amplitude = E3_ADORA1_amplitude
)

E4_ADORA1_vector_data <- data.frame(
  Condition = "E4",
  acrophase = E4_ADORA1_acrophase,
  amplitude = E4_ADORA1_amplitude
)

# Combine the two data frames into a single one
combined_ADORA1_vector_data <- rbind(E3_ADORA1_vector_data, E4_ADORA1_vector_data) %>%
  arrange(desc(amplitude))


# --- 1. Create the Main Plot ---
max_amplitude <- max(combined_ADORA1_vector_data$amplitude, na.rm = TRUE)

# maximum radius
r_max <- max_amplitude * 1.5  
# Ring radii (we’ll force these as the y breaks so legend + rings match)
ring_r <- pretty(c(0, r_max), n = 4)
ring_r <- ring_r[ring_r >= 0]
zt_breaks <- seq(0, 22, by = 2)  # match your x breaks
ring_r <- ring_r[ring_r <= r_max] # prevents the geom_hline warning

# Function to generate wedge polygons for polar coordinates
make_wedge <- function(start, end, r, n_points = 200) {
  # Generate angles (in hours) for the arc, including start and end
  theta <- seq(start, end, length.out = n_points + 2)  # +2 to include start and end explicitly
  # Radius values from 0 to r_max, repeated for the arc, and back to 0
  r_vals <- c(0, rep(r, n_points), 0)
  # Create data frame for the closed polygon
  data.frame(
    x = theta[c(1, 1:n_points, n_points + 2)],  # Start, arc points, end
    y = r_vals  # From 0 to r_max and back to 0
  )
}

day_poly   <- make_wedge(0, 12, r_max)
night_poly <- make_wedge(12, 24, r_max)

main_plot_with_legend <- ggplot(combined_ADORA1_vector_data, aes(color = Condition)) +
  # Draw the day and night background ribbons
  geom_polygon(data = day_poly, aes(x = x, y = y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#FFFACD", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_polygon(data = night_poly, aes(x = x, y = y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#E6E6FA", alpha = 0.9) +
 # ZT spokes ON TOP of ribbons
geom_vline(xintercept = zt_breaks,
           inherit.aes = FALSE,
           color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +
   # ---- Rings ON TOP of ribbons (but still under arrows/icons) ----
geom_hline(yintercept = ring_r[ring_r > 0],
           color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Arrows are drawn based on their order in the arranged data frame
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = acrophase, y = 0, xend = acrophase, yend = amplitude),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  # Add the sun and moon symbols as annotations
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = max_amplitude * 1.4, label = "\u2600", size = 8) +
  annotate("text", x = 18, y = max_amplitude * 1.4, label = "\U0001F319", size = 8) +
  coord_polar(theta = "x", start = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 24), breaks = seq(0,22, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, r_max), breaks = ring_r) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("E3" = "black", "E4" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "ADORA1 Gene Group Acrophase Comparison (E3 vs. E4)",
    x = "Zeitgeber Time (ZT)", y = "Amplitude", color = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_void() + # Start with a completely blank theme
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black"),      
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5),
    # Keep spokes if you like, but remove theme-based rings
panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85"),
panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

# --- 2. Create the separate amplitude legend plot ---

# Build the main plot to extract the actual y-axis (radial) breaks
plot_build_data <- ggplot_build(main_plot_with_legend)
radial_breaks <- plot_build_data$layout$panel_params[[1]]$r.major

# Filter out the break at 0, as we don't need a ring for it
legend_rings <- data.frame(r = radial_breaks[radial_breaks > 0])

# Determine the maximum radius for setting the y-limit of the legend plot
legend_max_val <- if (length(legend_rings$r) > 0) max(legend_rings$r) else 0

amplitude_legend_plot <- ggplot() +
  # Draw circles for each break value found in the main plot
  geom_circle(data = legend_rings, aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = r), color = "grey50")+
  # Add text labels for each circle
  geom_text(data = legend_rings, aes(x = 0, y = r, label = r), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  theme_void() + 
  coord_fixed() +
  # Set ylim to ensure the largest ring and its text aren't cut off
  ylim(-legend_max_val, legend_max_val * 1.2)


# --- 3. Prepare the components for the final layout ---

main_plot_only <- main_plot_with_legend + theme(legend.position = "none")
condition_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(main_plot_with_legend)

# --- 4. Arrange the final figure in a three-column layout ---
final_plot <- grid.arrange(
  amplitude_legend_plot,
  main_plot_only,
  condition_legend,
  ncol = 3,
  widths = c(1.5, 5, 1.5)
)

# Set the working directory to the folder where you want to save PDFs
# Use ggsave() to save the plot as a high-quality PDF
rayleigh_dir <- here("Rayleigh Plots")
# Create the directory if it does not exist
if (!dir.exists(rayleigh_dir)) dir.create(rayleigh_dir)  
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(rayleigh_dir, "ADORA1 E3 and E4_Plot.pdf"),  
  plot = final_plot,
  width = 8,   # Width in inches
  height = 5,  # Height in inches
  device = cairo_pdf,
  # Add this line to specify the font
  family = "Segoe UI Symbol" 
)
```
